grammar.title: Reflexive Verbs in Daily Routines
grammar.explanation:
Many daily routine verbs in Spanish are reflexive, meaning the action is performed on oneself. They use reflexive pronouns:

• me (myself) - me despierto, me ducho
• te (yourself) - te despiertas, te duchas
• se (himself/herself) - se despierta, se ducha
• nos (ourselves) - nos despertamos
• se (themselves) - se despiertan

The reflexive pronoun goes before the conjugated verb: Me levanto a las siete.
With infinitives, it attaches to the end: Voy a ducharme. Or: Me voy a duchar.

Note: despertar becomes 'despertarse' (reflexive), and the stem changes: e → ie (me despierto).
